titulo: What Is the Polar Vortex Weather System?

fuente.licencia: Dominio público (VOA, gobierno de EE. UU.)
fuente.nota: Texto recortado por párrafos; sin cambios en las frases.

parrafos: Weather experts say extreme cold in many parts of the United States this winter has been driven by a polar vortex. But what is this weather system and how does it work?
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) describes a polar vortex as strong westerly winds that form each winter in the atmosphere above the North Pole.
These cold winds move about 16 to 48 kilometers above the surface in the Arctic area in the part of the atmosphere called the stratosphere.
At times, the polar vortex can weaken, causing masses of cold air to break off and move south. A polar vortex can also push warmer air in northerly directions.

The Associated Press (AP) reports that several vortex events have affected parts of the U.S. this winter. Experts say weather forces in the Arctic have combined to push colder air to the U.S. and Europe.

Temperature readings that take into account the effects of wind, called windchill readings, fell to minus 51 degrees Celsius in parts of the U.S. Midwest. Meteorologists say windchill readings are colder than air temperature readings.

The U.S. National Weather Service (NWS) warned people in affected areas that such low temperatures can cause frostbite and hypothermia if skin is not protected from the cold. Weather officials also warned that long-term cold temperatures can cause water pipes in or around homes to freeze and burst.

The NWS noted that almost every U.S. state – except for Hawaii, California and Florida – is expected to report low windchill temperatures. The coldest temperatures were expected in the midwestern states of Kansas, Nebraska and Missouri.
In an explanation on its website, NOAA states that the polar vortex always surrounds both of Earth’s poles. The systems strengthen in the winter and weaken in the summer.

Every year or so, the polar vortex becomes weaker. This can cause the system to be “pushed off the pole or split into two.” This can lead to cold air at the surface being pushed southward and warm air being pushed to the north.

NOAA says its weather models are predicting low temperatures for states including Oklahoma, Colorado, Nebraska, Missouri, Illinois and Iowa. Other states likely to have very low temperatures are Wyoming, Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Michigan.
resumen_es: El texto explica qué es el vórtice polar, por qué su debilitamiento envía masas de aire ártico hacia el sur y qué consecuencias ha tenido en un invierno de frío extremo en Estados Unidos.

ideas_clave.idea: The extreme cold in the U.S. this winter has been attributed to the polar vortex, a band of strong westerly winds that forms every winter in the stratosphere above the North Pole.
When the vortex weakens, masses of freezing air can escape southwards, and several such episodes this winter sent cold air to the U.S. and Europe.
Windchill temperatures dropped to minus 51 degrees Celsius in the Midwest, and the authorities warned of frostbite, hypothermia and burst water pipes.
Nearly every state except Hawaii, California and Florida was expected to record low windchill readings, especially Kansas, Nebraska and Missouri.
NOAA explains that a vortex always surrounds both poles, growing stronger in winter, and that roughly once a year it weakens, shifts or splits, sending cold air south and warm air north.
Forecasts predicted very low temperatures for a long list of central and northern states.

resumen_modelo: The text explains the polar vortex, the weather system behind this winter's extreme cold in the United States. According to NOAA, it consists of strong westerly winds that circle the poles in the stratosphere and intensify in winter. Whenever the vortex weakens, shifts or splits, Arctic air can be pushed southwards while warmer air moves north. Several such episodes have recently affected the U.S. and Europe, with windchill readings falling to minus 51 degrees Celsius in the Midwest. Consequently, the authorities warned of frostbite, hypothermia and frozen pipes, and forecast very low temperatures across most of the country.

preguntas.pregunta: How does NOAA describe a polar vortex?
opciones: As strong westerly winds above the North Pole
As a storm that forms over the ocean in summer
As a mass of warm air moving north
As a layer of ice covering the Arctic
respuestas: As strong westerly winds above the North Pole
preguntas.cita: describes a polar vortex as strong westerly winds that form each winter in the atmosphere above the North Pole
preguntas.explicacion: La NOAA lo define como fuertes vientos del oeste que se forman cada invierno sobre el Polo Norte. No es una tormenta oceánica ni una capa de hielo; el aire cálido hacia el norte es una consecuencia posible, no la definición.

preguntas.explicacion: Los vientos circulan a entre 16 y 48 kilómetros de altura, en la estratosfera, no a unos cientos de metros.

preguntas.cita: Temperature readings that take into account the effects of wind, called windchill readings
preguntas.explicacion: La sensación térmica («windchill») tiene en cuenta el efecto del viento. Nieve, humedad y altitud no se mencionan.

preguntas.pregunta: What risks did the National Weather Service warn about?
respuestas: It warned that the extreme cold could cause frostbite and hypothermia in people whose skin was not protected, and that prolonged cold could make water pipes freeze and burst.

preguntas.explicacion: El párrafo 6 menciona dos tipos de riesgo: para la salud (congelación, hipotermia) y para las viviendas (tuberías que se congelan y revientan).

preguntas.pregunta: According to NOAA, when do the polar vortex systems weaken?
preguntas.cita: The systems strengthen in the winter and weaken in the summer.
preguntas.explicacion: Los sistemas se refuerzan en invierno y se debilitan en verano. Además, el vórtice rodea los dos polos, no solo el sur.

preguntas.explicacion: El texto no menciona el cambio climático: solo dice que el vórtice se debilita aproximadamente cada año.

preguntas.pregunta: Why can a weaker polar vortex bring very cold weather to regions further south?
respuestas: Because when the vortex weakens it can be pushed away from the pole or split in two, and then the cold air near the surface is pushed southwards while warm air moves north.
preguntas.cita: This can lead to cold air at the surface being pushed southward and warm air being pushed to the north.
preguntas.explicacion: Los párrafos 3 y 9 explican el mecanismo: un vórtice debilitado deja escapar el aire frío hacia el sur.
